A1C Monitoring
A1C tests should be done at least twice a year in persons who are 
meeting treatment goals and have stable glycemic control. They 
should be done quarterly in persons whose therapy has changed 
or who are not meeting glycemic goals. In persons without dia-
betes A1C values are 4% to 6%. These values correspond to 
mean plasma glucose levels of approximately 70 to 126 mg/dl 
(3.9 to 7.0 mmol/L). Correlation between A1C levels and aver-
age glucose levels recently have been verified. An A1C of 6% re-
flects an average glucose level of 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L). 
Lowering A1C to below or around 7% is a reasonable goal for 
many nonpregnant adults with diabetes. An A1C less than 7% 
has been shown to reduce cardiovascular complications of dia-
betes and is associated with long-term reduction of macrovascu-
lar disease (ADA, 2014b). Less stringent goals, such as less than 
8% may be appropriate for individuals with advanced macro-
